description:
FILED s473t5a (#1501 CHECK 1 round 2, 2026-09-13).  #1581 is FIXED (the
package-block `my` no longer refuses the file), and the transpile now reaches a
different refusal, so t/op/goto.t stays TRANSPILE-FAIL at P 132/2, C 0/0.

    $ ./pl2cl < t/op/goto.t
    Parser2 TODO: forward goto to a standalone label

THE SITE (instrumented -- a temporary `warn` at Pl/Parser2.pm:9538 printing
`$lbl` and the offending sibling): the label is **label2** (t/op/goto.t:48) and
the earlier sibling that textually targets it is the `while ($?) { … } continue
{ … }` loop at lines 28-42, whose body holds `goto label2;`.

THE SURPRISE, and the reason this is its own task rather than "goto.t needs
general forward goto": the SAME label is handled at line-prefix 78 and refused
at 79.  Measured by prefix (`head -n N t/op/goto.t | ./pl2cl`):

    N = 47, 48, 49, 54, 55, 60, 70, 78   -> transpiles
    N = 79                               -> "forward goto to a standalone label"

Line 79 is `FINALE:` -- a standalone label with an EMPTY remainder.  So adding a
LATER standalone label changes whether the #63 catch-wrap claims the EARLIER
one: `delete $self->{_goto_caught}{refaddr($first)}` comes back false for
label2 once FINALE: is present, and the textual scan over earlier siblings then
finds the while loop's `goto label2` and gates.  That is a bug in the
catch-wrap's marking, not (only) a missing feature: the same file with the same
label pair compiles or refuses depending on a label 30 lines further down.

WHERE TO LOOK: `Pl/Parser2.pm`'s standalone-label branch in `_lower_block`
(around line 9515-9560) and whatever sets `_goto_caught` (the task-#63
catch-wrap).  Read the branch's comment first: it explains why a FORWARD goto
is gated (its `(go …)` is emitted before the tagbody opens, where CL cannot
reach the tag) and which forward shapes the catch-wrap does handle.

DO NOT RETRY: making the standalone-label branch accept the forward case by
widening the textual scan.  The scan is not the bug -- the marking is; a wider
scan gates MORE files, and a narrower one emits a `(go …)` with no reachable
tag, which is a load-time CL error, not a perl-shaped one.

SIZE: 134 rows (the whole file).  t/op/goto.t is a deliberate goto maze -- it
has ten labels and 14 `goto`s at file level -- so it is the right acceptance
test for the forward-goto work, and a poor first target.  A cheaper first step
is the prefix table above: find why FINALE: un-marks label2.
subject: t/op/goto.t's SECOND blocker, uncovered when #1581 shipped -- "Parser2 TODO: forward goto to a standalone label" for `label2:` when a later standalone label exists; all 134 rows still lost
